The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$α$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.

papers.title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
papers.abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.

papers.title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
papers.abstract: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

papers.title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
papers.abstract: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($ε_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $ε_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $ε_{\rm ff}-Σ_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $ε_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $ε_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log Σ_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $ε_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

papers.title: Exploring Case B I: The Footprints of Hidden Radiation Fields in H I Balmer Decrements
papers.abstract: Theory predicts that H I emission from photoionized clouds should lie close to the Case B limit established by Menzel and Baker, and observations of nearby nebulae have largely confirmed this expectation. However, recent observations of more distant high-redshift systems have revealed a small fraction with striking departures from Case B. What additional physics might be at work in these objects? This paper is part of a series exploring the physical processes that can produce such departures. In Paper I (D26), we show that Case B remains remarkably robust over a broad range of physical conditions, consistent with observations of nearby nebulae. Here, we explore one additional ingredient: a soft, non-ionizing radiation field. Such a continuum can strongly perturb the Balmer spectrum. The largest effects occur for radiation fields resembling log(Teff K)\sim 3.2-4.2 blackbodies, where photoexcitation from the metastable 2s level alters the hydrogen level populations and subsequent radiative cascade. The resulting Halpha/Hbeta and Hgamma/Hbeta ratios follow a different trajectory from dust reddening, allowing the two effects to be distinguished using multiple Balmer lines. In unresolved systems, a cool source located near the line-emitting gas may provide an additional radiation field distinct from the hot stars responsible for ionization. Balmer decrements may therefore carry information about otherwise hidden components of the radiation field surrounding the emitting gas.

papers.title: The GAPS programme at TNG LXXXII. The first atmospheric investigation of the gas giant WASP-13b at high resolution with GIARPS
papers.abstract: Low-density transiting gas giant exoplanets are key benchmarks for atmospheric studies. Despite their large-scale heights, many of them remain poorly characterised. We present the first atmospheric investigation at high-resolution of the inflated (R$_\mathrm{p}$$\sim$1.4 R$_{\mathrm{J}}$), hot Jupiter (T$\sim$1500$ \mathrm{K}$) WASP-13 b aiming at constraining its atmospheric composition and refine its orbital geometry. We analysed four transits observed with GIARPS at the TNG. Updated stellar and planetary parameters were re-derived from the most precise literature values, and a new Rossiter-McLaughlin analysis was performed to measure the projected spin-orbit angle ($λ$) and stellar rotational velocity ($v\sin{i_\star}$). Atmospheric signals were searched using high-resolution spectroscopy, both with cross-correlation and single-line analyses, targeting key atomic and molecular species (e.g. \ion{He}{I}, H$α$, \ion{Na}{I}, H$_2$O, CO). We find a well-aligned orbit ($λ$ = 2.7$\pm$1.1$^\circ$) and $v\sin{i_\star}$ = 4.5$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$, improving upon previous constraints. No significant atmospheric absorption is detected in either VIS or NIR data. Injection-and-recovery tests exclude an isothermal atmosphere with metallicity [M/H]$\lesssim$10$\times$[M/H]$_\odot$ and simultaneously a grey cloud top pressure P$_{\rm cloud}\gtrsim10$ mbar, under the assumption of chemical equilibrium. WASP-13 b appears to belong to the class of low-density hot Jupiters with weak or featureless transmission spectra, most likely shaped by the presence of high-altitude clouds. Although a highly metal-enriched atmosphere cannot be fully excluded, current evidence disfavours this scenario. Further observations with next-generation facilities will be essential to characterise the atmospheric properties of this challenging target.

papers.title: Dust-driven vertical shear instability in an isothermal shearing box: I. Turbulence and gas dynamics without dust feedback
papers.abstract: The classical vertical shear instability (VSI) is a baroclinic instability that arises from height-dependent azimuthal velocities and is a leading candidate for driving anisotropic turbulence in discs with extended vertical modes. The classical VSI requires fast cooling times and radial temperature gradients, which are absent in an isothermal stratified (barotropic) setup. We investigate the dust-driven vertical shear instability in an isothermal, stratified shearing box, where the VSI is generated by drag forces acting on the gas due to dust rather than radial thermal stratification. We construct two-fluid (gas+dust) vertically stratified equilibria including dust diffusion and use these profiles to initialise 2D (radial-vertical) hydrodynamical simulations with FARGO3D. To separate dust-driven vertical shear instability (DVSI) from drag instabilities, we employ a dust-analogue model in which dust-induced drag on the gas is prescribed as a time-invariant and height-dependent acceleration, such that the underlying spatial distribution of the dust is assumed to be constant. The DVSI grows from regions of strongest vertical shear away from the midplane, exciting predominantly radially short, vertically extended disturbances (large k_x/k_z) and producing banded structures in the perturbed azimuthal and vertical velocities during the linear phase. In the nonlinear regime, the instability saturates via a Kelvin-Helmholtz-like parasitic instability that breaks the coherent vertical-shear modes into smaller-scale eddies, which balance the growth of the vertically extended modes, driving sustained vertical stirring. Dust-driven vertical shear can drive anisotropic turbulence and vertical mixing in an isothermal model without invoking global thermal gradients and could play an important role in the stratified streaming instability.

papers.title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
papers.abstract: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$α$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$α$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.

papers.title: "Mega-Earths" are likely an artifact of stellar activity
papers.abstract: Empirical relations and planet formation simulations suggest an upper mass limit for rocky planets of $\sim$10M$_{\oplus}$, as cores above this will almost certainly undergo runaway gas accretion. Nevertheless, a small number of planets appear to have densities consistent with rocky Earth-like compositions above this threshold, indicating that unusual formation and evolutionary scenarios are capable of producing extremely massive rocky planets called "Mega-Earths." However, all of these planets orbit active stars with log$R'_{HK}$ $>$-4.75. We find a <1$\%$ probability that all literature ultra-massive rocky planets would coincidentally orbit such active stars, and find no astrophysical reason to expect Mega-Earths to preferentially form around active stars. We therefore conclude that Mega-Earths are artifacts of stellar activity, and we question the reliability of Gaussian Processes to enable mass measurements for rocky planets around active stars.

papers.title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
papers.abstract: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $Ω_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.

papers.title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
papers.abstract: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.

papers.title: The road to $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
papers.abstract: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_ν\propto L_X^β$) will reach $β=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5σ$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $β=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

papers.title: Seeing in the Dark: Gravitational Waves from Resonant Production of Dark Photon Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark photons (DPs) are well-motivated dark matter candidates. A promising yet underexplored mechanism for their relic abundance is parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model that generates the DP mass. We advance previous analytical studies through dedicated 3D lattice simulations that capture important nonlinear effects, including backreaction and relic partitioning between the dark Higgs and DPs. We further predict the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal, which can be within reach of a broad range of detectors, opening a new avenue to probe ultralight DP dark matter.

papers.title: The accretionally heated atmospheres of protoplanets and brown dwarfs
papers.abstract: The ranks of accreting planets and brown dwarfs are growing. To help interpret their spectra, we study how accretion affects a planet's atmosphere. The atmosphere is irradiated from above by whatever nonthermal radiation from the accretion shock does not directly escape into space. This accretional heating drives a temperature inversion. Even relatively slow accretion, corresponding to mass doubling times longer than system ages, can raise temperatures by many hundreds of Kelvin at ambient pressures of order millibars. The heated atmosphere radiates an optical/infrared excess. For environments that are not too dusty, the excess concentrates in molecular lines that trace the heated layer. Thus an accretionally heated atmosphere may be distinguished by its muted absorption bands. Irradiation from the accretion shock also changes the chemical composition of the atmosphere, further altering spectra. Atmospheric retrievals promise to map out the deposition of accretional energy, helping to decide between ''hot'' and ''cold'' start modes of planet formation.

papers.title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
papers.abstract: Primordial overdensities at small scales can be significantly larger than those observed at large scales. As a result, they can collapse much earlier, at redshifts $z \sim 100$. In these collapsed halos, stars and black holes can form, where they can then contribute to an early reionization of the universe. If this epoch is temporary, the free electrons will recombine yielding a low level of ionization leading into cosmic dawn. This contributes to the optical depth of the universe, and adds more weakly to low-$\ell$ polarization signals of ionization compared to later sources. We study the effects of a redshift-localized source of reionization $Δτ_{burst}$ in the context of a broad suite of cosmological data to constrain this scenario, finding a preference of approximately $\sim 2-2.5σ$ for a new contribution. Regardless of Planck reprocessing used (PR3 - SRoll2+plik or PR4 - LoLLiPoP+CamSpec/HiLLiPoP), the results are consistent, favoring a new contribution $Δτ_{burst} \sim 0.012$ ($0.001 < Δτ_{burst} < 0.022$ at 95\%) and a similar total optical depth $τ\sim 0.073$. The precise era of reionization is somewhat discrepant depending on the higher-$\ell$ reprocessing used, with HiLLiPoP favoring $z\sim 45$, CamSpec $z\sim 100$ and plik $z\sim 165$. If such a source is present at $40\lesssim z\lesssim150$, LiteBIRD should be able to detect it, while Simons Observatory should also constrain it.

papers.title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm μm$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0$Å, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620Å on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$α$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$α$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.

papers.title: General Spin-1 Dynamics During Inflation: Microcausality Constraints and Cosmological Collider Signals
papers.abstract: We construct the general theory of a spin-1 field propagating on an inflationary background consistent with scale invariance, rotations, Bunch-Davies conditions and microcausality. Our Boostless Proca theory generalises the usual massive Proca theory to a Lagrangian with 5 free parameters: 4 corresponding to parity-even terms and a single parity-odd term. We impose three degrees of freedom from the outset and find that microcausality, the statement that field operators vanish outside the lightcone, requires the kinetic terms to be gauge invariant. We couple this spin-1 state to the inflaton and study the signatures it imprints on cosmological correlators. We find no new signals for the bispectrum meaning that the known signals are the most general thereby providing a very clean model-independent probe of new physics in this leading form of non-Gaussianity. For the trispectrum and higher-point functions, the boostless Proca theory produces new shapes with all 5 parameters in principle measurable.
